items.response:
A beagle snore that gets mistaken for a power drill is a real talent, and Diego will be telling that one for a while. Hope you still get the slow evening you earned.
Action: Nothing needed from you; I'll leave Biscuit to his nap.

That is a classic beagle invoice: either lunch is overdue or he heard a crinkle somewhere. He clearly believes the debt is serious.
Action: Nothing to do; Aisha's retry comments stay queued for when you're back in the doc.

Good plan on the cousin, and I'm glad to be the distraction. For a single architect who bikes everywhere and likes old buildings, I'd point Priya to the Annex (big old houses, Bloor bike lane), Little Portugal or Trinity Bellwoods (Victorian rowhouses, Dundas and Ossington lanes), and Cabbagetown (the best preserved Victorian streets, a short ride to the core). Corktown/Distillery is the pick only if she wants converted lofts. Where her firm's office would be matters, so I'd narrow it once she knows.
Action: I'll stay on standby; tell me when the cousin answers and I'll draft any follow-up texts to your mom.

Pastel de nata comes from Lisbon, specifically Belem, where monks at the Jeronimos Monastery made them before the 1800s, and a bakery nearby has sold them from the monastery recipe since 1837. For Leo: 'Monks used egg yolks left over from starching clothes with egg whites, so they made custard tarts with them.' The cinnamon and the burnt blistered top are the classic details.
Action: If Leo wants more, I can find a bakery in Toronto that sells them or a simple kid-friendly recipe to try.

Sure, let's get them sorted. I don't have your notes open in this conversation, so I'll pull them rather than guess.
Action: Search your notes app for everything created or edited this month, list titles with dates, and suggest groupings (keep, merge, archive) for you to approve before I change anything.

I don't have next week's calendar in front of me, so I'd rather pull it than give you a partial rundown.
Action: Check the family and work calendars plus school notices for next week and send a day-by-day list, with any conflicts flagged.

Noted: no replacement for the 2019 Mazda CX-5 in 2026, the money goes to the kitchen renovation, and we revisit an EV in 2028. I'll stop those trade-in emails.
Action: Find the dealer's emails, use their unsubscribe link and send an opt-out request for marketing, then set a filter so any future ones skip your inbox. I'll confirm once the unsubscribe goes through.

Good to know Jun is fine and nobody needs a thing from you there. On the clash, I'll ask Olivia to move 'QBR prep' to 11:00 so it stops overlapping your 10:00-10:50 roadmap check-in. For Ellie, I've noted she's allergic to dairy, but I don't have a pantry list here, so I'll check what we actually have before suggesting snacks.
Action: Message Olivia asking for 11:00 and look through the recent grocery orders to list dairy-free snacks for Ellie and Jun before they arrive after school.

For the sync opener, keep it clean and workplace-safe, no crypto. Something like: 'My budget and I have a lot in common, we both look great on paper and fall apart in reality.' For the open evening, a low-effort option is a home dinner you cook together plus a movie or game, or a takeaway night with a walk first.
Action: Pull your saved 'standup openers' backups from notes so you can pick one, and check the calendar for anything that edges into that evening.

The offsite is Thu 12 Nov. I'll count business days from tomorrow up to the day before, skipping weekends and any holidays, and tell you whether I counted the offsite day itself.
Action: Run the count and send the number, along with what's still due before then (memo comments to Tom, the Q1 page) so you can see the runway.

That is a lot of bending in one week, and it's fair to be fed up: protected Tuesday morning gone and a day trip dropped on you with notice. Once the trip is booked we can also look at whether to say something to Tom about the Tuesday move. For Montreal on Thu the 8th, I'll look at trains and flights that get you out in the morning and back for dinner.
Action: Search Toronto-Montreal options for Thu 8th with morning departures and evening returns, then send the best two with times and prices. I won't book until you pick.

Booking Ascari for Sat 16 Aug at 19:00, party of 5, which also fits your rule of 19:00 with good vegetarian options. They have kids' butter pasta and margherita for Leo. For Thanksgiving, I'll price Toronto to Vancouver for the three of you from Oct 10 to 13.
Action: Book Ascari Enoteca for 19:00 and confirm, then search flights for three, Oct 10 to 13, and send options without booking.

Will do. Suggested new message: 'Hi, I'm back but still catching up on email, so replies may take a little longer. Best, Riya'.
Action: Turn the out-of-office off for tomorrow morning, swap in that message, and show you the final text and end time to confirm.

Fine to leave Tom until after dinner. His message is still waiting and I don't have the beta merchant numbers link saved, so I'll keep it on your list for tonight.
Action: Check your library account for holds that are ready and loans due this week, and send the pickup branch, hold-until dates and due dates.

That is frustrating, especially with calls dropping. I'll check whether there's a known outage for your area first, then open a ticket so it's on record before the weekend.
Action: Find your provider from recent bills, check its outage page and status, then open a ticket noting two dropped calls this afternoon and that you need it stable before the weekend. I'll send you the ticket number.

I don't want to guess at Ottawa's actual weather for that day. I'll check observed data so you and Grace can settle it with real numbers.
Action: Look up Environment Canada's observed conditions for Ottawa on the 25th, including high, low, wind chill and snowfall, and send them. I'll confirm the month with you if it's unclear.

COUNTIF is enough: =COUNTIF(D:D,">10000") counts payouts over $10,000. If you want 10,000 itself included, use ">=10000". It ignores the header text, and your library holds close at 20:30 tonight if you pass by on your way out.
Action: None needed unless you want me to put that formula into a specific sheet.

Sure, I'll try for Apr 22 late morning with Dr. Lin. I'll also confirm it's your own cleaning, not Leo's.
Action: Check Dr. Lin's office for Apr 22 slots around 10:30 to 12:00, book the best one, add it to your calendar, and include the confirmation in your evening digest rather than pinging you. If Apr 22 is full I'll send the nearest alternatives.

Two is the correct number and no regrets is the right attitude, especially in an arctic office. A warm custard tart is a fine way to get through an afternoon.
Action: None; the retro RSVPs and Miro numbers stay as I last gave them.

Last time you looked at East End Plumbing Co. (4.8, Queen St E) and Riverside Drain & Plumbing (24/7 emergency), and a frost-free hose bib was better than a washer fix. Those prices and openings are old, so I'll recheck. Meanwhile, shutting the tap off from the inside valve should stop the drip.
Action: Check current availability today and Monday for East End, Riverside and Coxwell, then send the earliest openings with prices for you to pick.

Classic Sam. Sleep well.
Action: None.

Five nut-free lunches for camp: turkey and cheese roll-ups with cucumber; pasta salad with cheddar cubes and peas; cheese quesadilla wedges with salsa; a chicken or hummus wrap with carrot sticks; yogurt with fruit and crackers. I'll flag any packaged items that say 'may contain tree nuts', and keep all nuts out regardless of the camp's policy. I don't have the Biscuit and ambulance conversation in front of me, so I won't guess what you asked.
Action: Search past chats and notes for Biscuit and the ambulance, then tell you what you asked so you can tell Leo.

Good news on the electrician coming Monday. I don't have the crew's contact or the electrician's arrival window here, so I'll check.
Action: Find the contractor's contact, message the kitchen crew that the electrician is coming Monday, and propose a start time that doesn't overlap with the electrician once I have his window. I'll send you the proposed time before I send anything.

Nice, that will help with Biscuit's days. Jess from Rover, noon on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays at $25 a walk is $75 a week, which is about $325 a month.
Action: Add a recurring Mon/Wed/Fri 12:00 event starting Monday, add a $75/week dog walker line to the pet budget, and tell you the new monthly total against the pet budget.

Here's a draft: 'Hi Hannah! Thank you so much for the shortbread, it was delicious. Leo ate four!'
Action: Send it to Hannah once you say go, or tell me what to tweak.

Rough start with the 40 minute bag wait, and forgetting his swim shirt and stuffie is exactly the kind of thing a list fixes. I don't have your packing preference saved, so I'd rather ask than guess.
Action: Ask how you'd like packing handled (who packs what, a list per person, a night-before check), and meanwhile draft a return-trip checklist with Leo's swim shirt and stuffie at the top.

Here's the full version for Carlos: 'Tres tristes tigres tragaban trigo en un trigal, en tres tristes trastos tragaban trigo tres tristes tigres.' Read it slowly first, then speed up, and watch the 'tr' blends. Launch week dread on Sunday night is normal, and a plan can help.
Action: I can set up a short Sunday evening wind-down and a Monday-morning checklist for launch week if you'd like. Say the word.

I don't have yesterday's route in front of me, so I won't make up a time. The Big Apple stop adds time too, so that may be part of why it felt long.
Action: Pull yesterday's route from our chat history, then compare the expected drive time with how long it actually took and send both.

Pickup is set and Sam can grab it. Here's the Slack draft: 'Quick reminder: the release freeze runs Thu 12:00 to Mon 09:00. Please get anything you need merged before Thursday noon, and ping Aisha if something urgent comes up. Thanks all!'
Action: Mark the store pickup for Sam, and save the Slack draft for you to post. I haven't posted anything.

Your notes 'Riya - Lisbon' and 'Lisbon Dec 2026' were updated, but I can't see their contents here, so I won't guess at the weather or packing.
Action: Open both notes and pull any weather or packing items for New Year's Eve; if nothing is there, I'll check a Lisbon forecast and typical December conditions and send a short packing list for Leo.

Good plan to label this weekend. Camp starts Mon 29 Jun, so here's a base list: water bottle, sunscreen, hat, closed-toe shoes or boots, a full change of clothes, a labelled bag and lunch. I'll check Riverdale Farm's own list so we don't miss anything specific to them.
Action: Find the camp's parent info for 29 Jun, merge it with my base list, and send a checklist with a 'label' column for the weekend.

Morning. I'll pull the blocked ones so you can see what's holding each.
Action: Pull your Linear tickets in a blocked state with the blocker and its owner, ordered by what you can clear fastest before standup next week.

Happy to surprise you. I'll build a family-style spread for three from Pai's menu, mixing a few shared dishes and rice with something mild for Leo, and keep the full total, tax, delivery and tip, under $100.
Action: Pull Pai's menu, build the order for 18:00 delivery, place it, and tell you what's coming and the total.

Poor Leo. Chipped front teeth are worth a quick look, so I'll ask Dr. Lin's office this week after school and say it was a fall on the monkey bars. If you can find the chip, keep it in milk.
Action: Check Dr. Lin's after-school openings this week, request the earliest, and check travel time from home to the office. I'll send the slot and drive time.

Added 'get passport photos for Leo' to your to-do list.
Action: None.

Sure, I'll pull Tom's calendar for the 24th. I'll assume last week's 24th unless you say otherwise.
Action: Check Tom's calendar, list his free slots that day, and note anything that explains why a pricing review couldn't fit.

I don't have the GA date, and my notes say nothing goes to Olivia or anyone in sales until Aisha Rahman has signed off, and drafts say 'target', not 'launch date'. I'll follow your style rules too, with no em dashes, 'merchant' not 'customer', and short paragraphs.
Action: Check Aisha's sign-off status in Slack and Linear. If she has signed off, draft the note with the target date; if not, draft a short message asking Aisha. Either way I'll show you first.

Sending the school council reply now. On insurance, starting 30 to 45 days before renewal is usually enough time to compare quotes. You can generally cancel any time with written notice, but make sure the new policy starts before the old one ends so there's no gap. Check your policy wording for any cancellation fee.
Action: Send the email, find the renewal date on the letter, and set a reminder to start quotes about 45 days before it.

My notes show last year's home insurance premium at $1,640 a year, which gives a baseline. I haven't seen this year's renewal yet, so I won't guess at the changes.
Action: Open the renewal notice and last year's policy, then send a side-by-side of premium, coverage limits, deductibles and any new exclusions or fees.

Happy to just talk, and no working kitchen for this long really does wear a person down. For the dust, don't sweep, since it just lifts it. Vacuum with a soft brush head with the beater bar off, then go over it with a barely damp microfiber mop, changing the cloth often. Dry any damp spots right away.
Action: I'm here for talking; tell me if you want me to look for a cleaner who handles post-reno dust or a timeline update on the kitchen.

No problem, I'll skim it. I'll give you the four items that affect you, with any deadlines or actions on you called out.
Action: Find this afternoon's all-hands email, summarise the four key points, and flag anything that needs a reply from you.

Your reminders have been set for Tuesday collection, but a holiday week can shift the schedule, so I'll check this week's City calendar before telling you.
Action: Look up this week's green bin and recycling day for your address, tell you the date, and adjust your bin reminder if it moved.

Sorry, that's annoying, especially with no note. Take photos of the scratch, dent and the lot now. The claim may be a hit-and-run, so I'll check your deductible against a repair quote first, since a small claim could cost more than it saves.
Action: Find your auto insurance policy and claims contact, draft the claim details (Loblaws lot, last night, rear bumper) and send it for your approval before I file anything.

On it. I'll book it as 25 minutes with the agenda in the invite: 1) empty-state copy, 2) loading skeleton, 3) who owns the Looker link.
Action: Find a morning next week when Aisha, Diego and you are all free, and book it with the three agenda items. I'll tell you the time.

On PEC, ask Sam tonight and I'll hold off. For the groceries, I'll build the cart at PC Express for Saturday morning pickup at Loblaws Lakeshore, 9:00 to 10:00, using no-name brands for staples.
Action: Build the cart with all your items, check the Saturday slot is open, and show you the total for approval before I check out.
